chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from Muhammad ibn Khalid Al-Qasri has been transmitted by me from has been transmitted by me from Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur - may Allah have mercy on him - from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Amir, from his uncle Abdullah ibn Amir, from Hafsah, from Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Abdullah Al-Bajali Al-Qasri, who was an Arab from Kufa.

key_terms.الْقَسْرِيُّ: Al-Qasri, a nisba indicating lineage or origin
key_terms.جَعْفَرُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مَسْرُورٍ: Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur, a key link in the chain
key_terms.عَرَبِيٌّ: Arab, indicating linguistic or tribal background
key_terms.كُوفِيٌّ: From Kufa, a major center of Shia scholarship
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ خَالِدٍ الْقَسْرِيُّ: Muhammad ibn Khalid Al-Qasri, a prominent narrator

ai.seo_question: How is the transmission chain for Muhammad ibn Khalid Al-Qasri verified in Shia hadith literature?
ai.summary: This passage from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* provides a specific *takhrij* (verification) of the isnad, linking Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Qasri—a prominent Kufi narrator—to the author, Shaykh al-Saduq, via Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur. By detailing this intermediate chain, al-Saduq reinforces the authenticity of the Kufi transmission tradition within the broader context of Twelver Shia hadith scholarship, ensuring the reliability of legal rulings derived from these narrations.
